Troubleshooting high CPU on Azure VMs
records.text:
Symptoms

Azure Monitor 'Percentage CPU > 90%' alert; application slowness.

Cause

Usually a single runaway process, a scheduled antimalware scan, or overlapping batch jobs.

Resolution

  1. Query Log Analytics: Perf | where CounterName == '% Processor Time' | top 10 by CounterValue
  2. Identify the top process and confirm with the app owner it is safe to restart
  3. Run runbook RB-VM-Restart-Service with parameter ServiceName
  4. If CPU stays > 85% after restart for 30 min, consider resizing the VM (raise a change)

Automation

Runbook: RB-VM-Restart-Service (safe to run automatically with approval)

Escalation

Resolver group: SKR Azure Infra Ops

records.short_description: Resolving low disk space on Azure VMs
records.text:
Symptoms

'Logical disk free space < 10%' alert; app errors writing files.

Cause

Unrotated logs, update caches, dumps or ETL extracts.

Resolution

  1. Identify largest folders (TreeSize / du -sh)
  2. Run RB-VM-Cleanup-Disk (deletes logs/temp older than 14 days, clears update cache)
  3. If data disk genuinely full, raise change to expand managed disk
  4. Ensure log rotation is configured

Automation

Runbook: RB-VM-Cleanup-Disk (safe to run automatically with approval)

Escalation

records.text:
Symptoms

Http5xx alert; users see HTTP 500/502/503.

Cause

Most often a bad release; sometimes a dependency (SQL, payments API) timing out.

  2. Check deployment history / recent changes on the app
  3. If release-related: run RB-AppService-SlotSwap-Rollback
  4. If dependency-related: check dependency health and engage owning team
  5. Restart the app (RB-AppService-Restart) only as last resort

records.text:
Symptoms

DTU > 95% alert; query timeouts in the app.

Cause

Expensive queries (often missing indexes) or periodic reporting load.

Resolution

  1. Open Query Store > Top resource consuming queries
  2. Run RB-SQL-Scale-Up to move one tier up (temporary, auto-reverts after 24 h)
  3. Raise a problem / change for index tuning if the same query recurs

records.text:
Symptoms

Blocked process alert; app/report hangs.

Cause

Long or uncommitted transactions holding locks.

Resolution

  1. Run sp_whoisactive / sys.dm_exec_requests to find head blocker
  2. Identify owner of the session; get approval before killing
  3. Kill session; check for rollback duration
  4. Human approval REQUIRED - do not automate kill without owner confirmation

Automation

records.short_description: SKR Change Management Policy
records.text:
Change types

  • Standard: pre-approved template, low risk, no CAB.
  • Normal: assessed by the change manager; high-risk changes go to the weekly CAB.
  • Emergency: restores service or fixes a critical security issue; approved by the emergency CAB (ECAB).

Required plans

Normal and emergency changes need an implementation plan, a backout plan and a test plan. A change with any of them empty, "N/A" or "TBD" is sent back to the requester. Normal changes are raised at least 48 hours before the planned start.

Maintenance windows (IST)

  • Tier-1 services (criticality 1): Tue, Thu and Sun 01:00-05:00.
  • All other services: daily 22:00-06:00.

Business hours (peak store and online trading): Monday to Friday 09:00-21:00 IST. Work in business hours carries the most customer impact.

Freeze periods

No normal or standard changes to production during a freeze (published as blackout schedules: sale events for all services; month-end finance close for Payments Integration, Order Processing and Data & Analytics). Only emergency changes, approved by the ECAB.

Risk

Risk is the likelihood that the change fails or causes an incident: Low below 10%, Moderate 10% to 18%, High 18% or more. Judge it from the service tier, what depends on the CI, the plans, the timing, conflicts, open problems and incidents, and how similar past changes went.

Approval by risk

  • Low: the change manager approves.
  • Moderate: the change manager approves with conditions (for example: move into the maintenance window, add a test step, have the resolver group on standby).
  • High: CAB review.

Conflicts

Changes that overlap in time on the same CI or a directly dependent CI must be re-sequenced or approved together.

Post-implementation review

Incidents on the changed CI or its dependents within 24 hours after the change are reviewed. Close codes: Successful; Successful with issues (incidents, no backout); Unsuccessful (backout executed or the change failed).
